Bimodal grain structures with coarse deformed grains and fine recrystallized (DRXed) grains were observed in the four as-extruded alloys.
The average DRXed grain sizes in the as-extruded 2.5Gd, 1.75Gd + 0.75Y, 1.25Gd + 1.25Y and 2.5Gd + 0.75Y alloys were about 3.3 μ m, 2.0 μ m, 2.2 μ m and 2.7 μ m, respectively.
The block-shaped phase with a white contrast is LPSO phase [16], which was arranged along the extrusion direction.
the nanoparticles are considered to be β -Mg5RE phase (fcc, a = 2.23 nm [22])

A larger number of microcracks at the grain boundaries were observed on the pre-polished surface in the small strain regions (Point 1). This may be the result of GB sliding during tensile test at 300 °C
The fine precipitates and LPSO phases are reported to contribute to the outstanding mechanical properties at elevated temperatures due to their high melting point and thermal stability
